newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks zigzag to close down in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks zigzag to close down in heavy trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks and index futures zigzagged throughout the day to close lower on Thursday as euphoria over the U.S. election was dampened by fears of profit-taking on Wall Street, brokers said.
"After the rallies yesterday, the Dow Jones and the Hang Seng are looking toppish," said a broker with a Swiss institution in Hong Kong.

The Hang Seng Index closed down 40.21 points at 12,735.26 after setting a new intraday high of 12,898.30 in early morning trade. Turnover was a strong HK$10.86 billion, besting Wednesday's HK$10.29 billion.
Brokers said turnover was boosted by an increase in programme trading by institutions and more speculative activity from the retail sector.

The November Hang Seng Index futures contract fell sharply by 55 points to close at 12,735, on a par with the cash market, with trade an active 18,007 contracts. It had soared for a day high of 12,905, nearing strong psychological resistance level at 13,000.

The Hang Seng Index put on more than 100 points shortly after the open, prompted by the Dow's 97-point gain to a record close of 6,177.71 on Wednesday, the New York market's single biggest one-day gain since March 18.

"It is a slightly bearish signal when the market moves to a new high then closes at a low, but I will only be worried if the index breaks below the 12,500 level," said Alan Shum, research manager at New Century Securities.
Chris Roberts, regional technical strategist at HSBC James Capel, said that he would encourage light profit-taking at this level.
"This is the least powerful bull market we have seen for years. Having said that I believe we are overdue for a correction, Roberts said.
He saw the key support level are 12,600 and 12,200.
The commercial and industrial sector was the best performing, while utilities were the most heavily sold.
Trading conglomerate Wheelock advanced HK$0.45 to HK$18.40, while Swire lost HK$1.25 to HK$67.50.
Index heavyweight Hongkong Telecom dropped HK$0.40 to HK$13.05, due to its lacklustre earnings outlook, brokers said.

New World Development fell HK$1.10 to HK$46.80. The company released its 1995/96 results showing a 21.89 percent rise, were a bit below expectations, said the broker. "But maybe the market's expectations were too aggressive."
